items.title: MLP Asia in Kuala Lumpur: the Dragon Warriors clinch a Finals spot, and the Viet Panthers sweep them 4-0 to retake first place
items.summary: The Dragon Warriors beat THE DOTS TOKYO 3-1 on Nov. 27 at Tomaz Pickleball Club in Kuala Lumpur to clinch a place in the MLP Asia Finals, which also put the Viet Panthers through, MLP Asia reported. Kong/Wei won women's doubles 11-4, Funemizu/Hatakeyama won men's doubles 11-9 for the DOTS, then Wei/Pham (11-5) and Kong/Goldin (11-8) took both mixed games. The Panthers then swept the Dragon Warriors 4-0 (Christian/Huynh 11-9, Shimabukuro/Truong 11-6, Shimabukuro/Christian 11-7, Huynh/Truong 11-3), their second 4-0 of the season, to finish the regular season first on 9 points. Standings per MLP Asia: Panthers 9 (done), Hong Kong Cannons 8 (one match left), Dragon Warriors 6 (done), THE DOTS TOKYO 5 (done), Malayan Stripes 2 (two left); Manila Helios are out. On the final night, Nov. 28 (6 PM local), the Stripes host the Cannons and then the Helios: any Cannons win makes them regular-season champions, and the Stripes take the last Finals spot only by winning both matches, or one in regulation and losing the other in a DreamBreaker; otherwise THE DOTS TOKYO go through. The Finals are Dec. 11-12.

items.title: Australia: 301,553 people played pickleball in 2025-26, Pickleball Australia estimates from AusPlay data, but that counts anyone who played once
items.summary: Pickleball Australia estimates that 301,553 Australians played pickleball in 2025-26, a figure drawn from AusPlay, the Australian Sports Commission's national participation survey, PIKL Australia and Times Now reported. AusPlay groups pickleball with padel, so Pickleball Australia applied pickleball's roughly 64% share of the combined figure across three years of data, and AusPlay counts anyone who took part at least once in the past 12 months, PIKL Australia explained. Pickleball Australia had 27,974 registered members on June 29, 2026, per PIKL Australia. PIKL's own estimate of about 90,000 regular players is an extrapolation from U.S. industry splits, not an AusPlay figure.

items.title: Are there really too few courts? An Arlington, Va. survey finds nearly 60% of public pickleball courts went unreserved Nov. 1-14
items.summary: Nancy Sharkey, a former member of Arlington County's Sports Commission, briefed the commission on Nov. 19 on her independent survey: nearly 60% of available county pickleball courts were not reserved on weekday evenings and weekends from Nov. 1 to 14, and on a Nov. 8 drive around the county she found 63% of courts in use by reservation or drop-in play, ARLnow reported Nov. 25. Arlington has 28 outdoor and 18 indoor courts striped for pickleball. In October the Arlington Pickleball Club had asked the commission to back a 'flagship' facility, possibly at Quincy Park. Commissioners urged caution about drawing conclusions from one snapshot. The Sports and Parks and Recreation commissions meet Dec. 8 on the Public Spaces Master Plan update; a final vote is set for early next year.

items.title: The Picklr bankruptcy: judge signs orders keeping club utilities on and approving Akerman and a chief restructuring officer, with a final utilities hearing Dec. 8
items.summary: Judge Scott W. Everett signed three orders in The Picklr's Subchapter V case on Nov. 25, per the docket. An interim utilities order (Dkt. 143) bars utility providers from cutting off or refusing service because of the bankruptcy or unpaid pre-filing bills, sets a $500-per-account adequate-assurance deposit on valid request, and schedules the final hearing for Dec. 8 at 1:30 p.m. CT. The court also approved hiring Akerman LLP as the debtors' attorneys (Dkt. 144) and Fuel Break Capital Partners as financial adviser, with Rick Rosenbloom as chief restructuring officer effective as of the petition date (Dkt. 145). Dec. 8 is already the date for the hearing on rejecting closed-club leases.

items.title: DUPR explains its new half-point rule: if the team rated 0.5 or more higher wins, nobody's rating moves
items.summary: In a Nov. 24 blog post, DUPR explained an algorithm change that went live Nov. 4 after a smaller test: when the two teams' average ratings are 0.5 or more apart and the higher-rated team wins, all four players' ratings stay unchanged regardless of the score. Upsets still move ratings, and inside a 0.5 gap ratings still move on performance against the expected score, so a narrow win can still cost points. DUPR says the rule covers singles and doubles, rally and traditional scoring, tournament and self-posted matches, and that players had been reluctant to record matches for fear a win would lower their rating. World Pickleball Magazine notes the flip side: in a half-point mismatch the underdog can no longer gain rating by losing close. Separately, DUPR announced a multi-year partnership with the Philippine Pickleball Federation the same day.

items.title: Pickleball England makes protective eyewear mandatory for under-18s at its competitions and strongly recommends it for adults
items.summary: Pickleball England's board approved a Protective Eyewear Policy on Nov. 19. Players under 18 must wear suitable impact-rated eyewear, warm-ups included, at Pickleball England-run and sanctioned competitions and at its junior events and festivals, even when playing in adult categories; a junior without it may not take part. For adults, eyewear is strongly recommended but optional unless an event, venue, club or insurer requires it. The policy says ordinary prescription glasses and sunglasses should not be assumed to protect. World Pickleball Magazine, which tied the policy to this week's BMJ glaucoma case report, says it is the only such requirement among the pickleball bodies it checked.

items.title: Doctors warn of pickleball eye injuries after a player hit without eyewear develops glaucoma
items.summary: A BMJ Case Reports paper by doctors at UMass Chan Medical School describes a woman in her early 50s who was hit directly in the left eye while playing pickleball without protective eyewear. She had blurred vision, severe pain and bleeding inside the eye (hyphema); three months later she had high eye pressure and optic nerve damage and was diagnosed with traumatic angle-recession glaucoma, which persisted despite surgery. The authors call it part of an emerging pattern of pickleball eye injuries, note that modern paddles can produce shots over 60 mph, and say sport-specific safety guidelines may be warranted. It is a single case report, not a study of injury rates.

items.title: The Picklr bankruptcy: judge signs the final DIP order approving up to $4.365 million in financing
items.summary: The U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Texas signed and entered the final DIP order in The Picklr's Subchapter V case on Friday, Nov. 13 (Dkt. 119), per the public docket kept by claims agent Omni. It lets Picklr, Inc. and Picklr Clubs borrow up to $4,365,000 in total, including $3.51 million in new-money term loans, with part of the debtors' prepetition bridge loans rolled into the facility, per the order. That follows the Nov. 10 final hearing. The same day the court entered an order letting the debtors pay taxes (Dkt. 120), and the debtors filed a new motion to reject a lease (Dkt. 122).
